title: CrashLoopBackOff container restarts
diagnostics: Inspect pod status and recent events
Read current and previous container logs
Compare deployment configuration with the last known-good revision
Check probe paths, ports, and timing
Check termination reason and resource usage
safety: Diagnose before restarting or rolling back; any production mutation requires operator approval.

title: Pods remain Pending
diagnostics: Review scheduler events
Compare resource requests with node allocatable capacity
Inspect affinity, selectors, taints, and tolerations
Check persistent volume claims
Check resource quotas
safety: Do not scale nodes or weaken scheduling constraints without capacity review and approval.

title: ImagePullBackOff
diagnostics: Inspect pod events for the registry error
Verify image reference and immutable digest
Check image pull secret association
Test registry reachability from the cluster network
Confirm node and image architecture compatibility
safety: Never expose registry credentials in logs or prompts; rotate credentials only through approved secret-management procedures.

title: Kubernetes Service has no reachable endpoints
likely_causes: Service selector does not match pods
diagnostics: Compare service selectors with pod labels
Inspect EndpointSlice objects
Verify readiness probes
Compare service target port with container port
Review relevant network policies
safety: Prefer read-only inspection; do not relax network policy in production without security approval.

title: CI build fails after dependency change
symptoms: Build works locally but not in CI
diagnostics: Compare CI runtime and package-manager versions
Verify lockfile is committed and enforced
Inspect registry and proxy errors
Run once with an isolated cache
Compare environment variables without printing secrets
safety: Do not disable integrity checks or expose registry tokens to troubleshoot the build.

title: Flaky tests in a deployment pipeline
symptoms: Failure rate rises under parallel execution
diagnostics: Measure failure frequency by test and runner
Capture timing and seed data
Run the suspected test in isolation and under repetition
Replace external dependencies with controlled fixtures
Check CPU, memory, and concurrency limits
safety: Quarantine with ownership and an expiry; do not silently remove quality gates.

title: Deployment rollout stalls
diagnostics: Inspect rollout status and events
Compare old and new replica health
Read new revision logs
Check readiness and startup probes
Verify surge and unavailable settings against capacity
safety: A rollback changes production and requires explicit operator approval after impact review.

title: Canary release shows elevated errors
symptoms: Latency regression limited to new version
diagnostics: Compare canary and baseline golden signals
Segment telemetry by version
Check schema and feature-flag compatibility
Inspect representative traces and errors
Verify traffic weights
safety: Pause promotion; rollback or traffic changes require operator approval and should follow the deployment runbook.

title: Terraform plan shows unexpected drift
symptoms: Plan changes resources with no expected code change
likely_causes: State is stale or points to wrong workspace
diagnostics: Confirm workspace, account, and region
Refresh state through the approved workflow
Review cloud audit history
Compare provider and module lock versions
Separate computed-only changes from real drift
safety: Do not apply an unexplained plan or edit state manually; obtain review and approval first.

title: Terraform state lock contention
diagnostics: Identify the lock owner and operation timestamp
Check active pipelines and operators
Verify backend availability
Confirm whether the owning process is still running
Follow backend-specific stale-lock recovery guidance
safety: Never force-unlock until ownership and inactivity are confirmed; unlocking or applying requires operator approval.

title: Container host disk pressure
likely_causes: Application data written to root disk
diagnostics: Measure filesystem and inode usage
Attribute usage to logs, images, layers, and volumes
Inspect log rotation configuration
Identify growth rate and affected workloads
Verify persistent data placement
safety: Deletion and pruning can destroy data; require explicit approval and verify retention requirements.

title: Cloud API throttling
diagnostics: Identify throttled API and account-region scope
Measure request and retry rates
Review service quotas
Trace callers and concurrency
Check retry strategy for jitter and caps
safety: Quota increases and controller changes should be reviewed for cost and blast radius.

title: Intermittent DNS resolution failures
symptoms: Services fail while direct IP checks pass
diagnostics: Measure lookup latency and response codes
Compare node and workload resolver configuration
Inspect DNS service saturation and errors
Test authoritative resolution separately
Review recent network-policy changes
safety: Do not replace resolver configuration globally without staged validation and approval.

title: TLS certificate expiry or chain failure
likely_causes: Wrong certificate served by load balancer
diagnostics: Inspect the served certificate chain and dates
Verify hostname coverage
Compare certificate at each proxy layer
Check renewal-controller events
Check system time and client trust assumptions
safety: Treat private keys as secrets; never paste them into logs, prompts, or tickets.

title: Prometheus target is down or metrics are missing
diagnostics: Inspect target status and last scrape error
Verify service discovery labels
Test metrics endpoint from the monitoring network
Review scrape timeout and payload size
Inspect relabeling decisions
safety: Avoid disabling TLS verification or authentication as a permanent fix.

title: Noisy or frequently flapping alert
diagnostics: Compare alert history with incidents
Measure signal variance and duration
Identify duplicate notifications
Validate labels and routing
Define an actionable symptom and owner
safety: Tune alerts using historical evidence; do not mute critical coverage without a time limit, owner, and approval.

title: Database connection pool exhaustion
diagnostics: Compare active, idle, and waiting connections
Inspect acquisition and query latency
Trace connection lifecycle in the application
Check slow queries and lock waits
Review retry volume and pool settings
safety: Restarting may provide only temporary relief and requires approval; preserve evidence before mutation.

title: Redis memory pressure and evictions
diagnostics: Inspect memory usage, fragmentation, and eviction counters
Sample key sizes without exposing values
Check TTL distribution
Compare growth with deploys and traffic
Review configured eviction policy
safety: Flushing keys or changing eviction policy can cause outages or data loss and requires explicit approval.

title: Kafka consumer lag increases
diagnostics: Segment lag by topic, partition, and consumer group
Compare consume rate with produce rate
Inspect rebalance and processing errors
Check broker and network latency
Identify repeatedly failing messages without exposing payload data
safety: Changing offsets can skip or duplicate processing; require explicit approval and a recovery plan.

title: Service latency regression
diagnostics: Compare golden signals before and after the regression
Use traces to locate the slow span
Segment by version, endpoint, region, and customer tier
Inspect dependency latency and saturation
Correlate with deployments and configuration changes
safety: Do not infer root cause from correlation alone; verify with multiple evidence sources before remediation.
